item.name: Porsche 911 flat-six engine
item.summary: Six cylinders. One continuous story of air, fuel, force and heat.

identity.notes: Chosen exemplar: early 1965 Type 901/01 architecture. Original educational reconstruction, not scanned OEM CAD.

modelNotice: 1965 flat-six · reference-guided reconstruction · dimensions & hidden details approximate
artNote: Original geometry authored for this open-source study from period diagrams and inspected engine photographs. The study includes 29 physical assemblies presented in 26 component lessons and four subsystem milestones; matching crankcase halves, heads and cylinder banks share their views. Casting contours, ports, tolerances, finishes and small hardware are approximate; it is not a repair or assembly guide. The external dry-sump tank, fuel supply, vehicle wiring, clutch/transmission and complete heat-exchanger system are outside the engine model. No downloaded Porsche or marketplace geometry is redistributed. Material appearance is inferred where an exact alloy or coating has not been established.
closing: Every breath becomes motion. Every part comes home.

sources.title: MS Road and Race: original 1965 aluminum chain-box covers
Restored 901/01: front and top reference photographs

components.name: Belt & pulleys
components.material: Machined metal pulleys · matte rubber belt
components.howItsMade: The crankshaft turns a belt. That belt drives the cooling fan and alternator, so the running engine provides its own airflow. Two grooved pulleys joined by a continuous belt; exposed hexagonal centre nuts. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Pulley diameters and belt cross-section are reference-fitted, not measured.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Pulley diameters and belt cross-section are reference-fitted, not measured.

components.name: Cooling fan
components.howItsMade: The pitched blades accelerate air into the shroud. Cooling needs directed flow across the hot surfaces, not simply an exposed engine. Eleven curved blades, tapered hub, solid blade edges and changing surface normals. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Blade pitch and aerofoil geometry are inferred from photographs.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Blade pitch and aerofoil geometry are inferred from photographs.

components.name: Fan housing
components.howItsMade: The housing supports the fan and alternator while keeping the blade tips close to the surrounding ring. It forms the inlet to the cooling duct. Open circular casting with lip, cylindrical barrel and rear support spokes. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Exact alloy and casting marks are not established.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Exact alloy and casting marks are not established.

components.name: Alternator
components.howItsMade: Behind the fan, an alternator converts shaft rotation into electrical power. It shares the belt drive rather than needing a second motor. Ribbed cylindrical housing nested behind the fan hub. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Internal windings and electrical circuit are outside this engine-mechanism study.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Internal windings and electrical circuit are outside this engine-mechanism study.

components.name: Cooling shroud
components.material: Satin black finish · no baked highlights
components.howItsMade: The black shroud guides fan air over both cylinder banks. Without that guidance, air could escape before collecting heat from the fins. Rounded hollow canopy with open underside, rear panel and side ducts. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Duct contours and wall thickness are approximate; coating chemistry is unverified.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Duct contours and wall thickness are approximate; coating chemistry is unverified.

components.name: Air cleaner
components.howItsMade: The air cleaner feeds the two banks of carburetors. Removing it reveals six separate intake throats beneath. Paired rounded housings with a connecting duct; a simplified early air-cleaner envelope. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Air-cleaner silhouette is less certain than the exposed engine; internal filter media is not reconstructed.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Air-cleaner silhouette is less certain than the exposed engine; internal filter media is not reconstructed.

components.name: Solex carburetors
components.material: Cast alloy bodies · machined throats · brass fittings
components.howItsMade: The early 901/01 uses Solex carburetion. Air passes through a throat for each cylinder; throttle position changes the flow and the carburetor meters fuel into it. Six open throats, flared entries, throttle discs and shafts, fuel chambers and brass fittings. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Jet passages, calibration, and fuel recirculation plumbing are not reproduced.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Jet passages, calibration, and fuel recirculation plumbing are not reproduced.

components.name: Intake manifolds
components.howItsMade: The intake runners connect the carburetors to the cylinder heads. An intake valve admits the mixture into the chamber at the appropriate part of the cycle. Six curved runners with flange rings and paired mounting studs. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Runner bends and wall thickness are reference-fitted.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Runner bends and wall thickness are reference-fitted.

components.name: Left cylinder heads
components.material: Cast light alloy · machined sealing faces
components.howItsMade: Each cylinder has its own head. The chamber closes the cylinder while the intake and exhaust valves control what enters and leaves. Three finned heads with chamber-closing faces, separate valve openings, seat rings and perimeter studs. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Combustion-chamber contours and port cross-sections are simplified.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Combustion-chamber contours and port cross-sections are simplified.

components.name: Right cylinder heads
components.material: Cast light alloy · machined sealing faces
components.howItsMade: The opposite three cylinders work through the same four-stroke sequence. Their horizontal arrangement gives the flat-six its broad, low form. Second set of three heads, staggered along the crankshaft to match the rods. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Bank spacing is illustrative, not a workshop measurement.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Bank spacing is illustrative, not a workshop measurement.

components.name: Left cylinder bank
components.material: Dark finned metal · smoother bore surface
components.howItsMade: The bore guides the piston. Outside, thin fins increase the surface exposed to cooling air; the hot cylinder can shed heat as the fan drives air past. Three hollow barrels with thirteen modeled fins each, bore walls and long head studs. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Fin count/spacing and cylinder metallurgy are visual approximations, not a verified part specification.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Fin count/spacing and cylinder metallurgy are visual approximations, not a verified part specification.

components.name: Right cylinder bank
components.material: Dark finned metal · metallic stud hardware
components.howItsMade: Three cylinders sit on each side of the crankcase. Opposed pistons move toward and away from the centre as their rods follow separate crankpins. Three opposing hollow barrels; no solid caps hiding the pistons. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: This is a static assembly pose, not a running-engine simulation.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. This is a static assembly pose, not a running-engine simulation.

components.name: Six pistons
components.material: Machined light metal · darker ring bands
components.howItsMade: Combustion pressure pushes on each piston crown. Rings seal against the bore while the hollow skirt and wrist pin connect that force to a rod. Six hollow-skirt pistons with crown discs, three ring bands and wrist pins. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Crown profiles, ring gaps, pin-bore details and clearances are approximate.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Crown profiles, ring gaps, pin-bore details and clearances are approximate.

components.name: Connecting rods
components.howItsMade: Each rod connects a piston pin to its own crankpin. The big end follows a circle while the small end follows the piston, converting reciprocation into rotation. Six rods with open big ends, small-end rings, web sections and cap hardware. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Forging contours and bearing clearances are simplified.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Forging contours and bearing clearances are simplified.

components.name: Crankshaft
components.material: Steel shaft · polished journals · darker webs
components.howItsMade: Six offset crankpins gather the piston forces into one rotating shaft. Main journals support it inside the case; counterweights help manage the rotating loads. Seven main journals, six separate crankpins, shaped counterweights and drive-end gear. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Throw layout is educational; balance, firing order and dynamic loads are not simulated.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Throw layout is educational; balance, firing order and dynamic loads are not simulated.

components.name: Flywheel
components.howItsMade: The flywheel stores rotational energy between firing impulses and passes torque toward the clutch. Its toothed perimeter also gives the starter a place to engage. Heavy circular disc, machined annulus, bolted hub and separate ring-gear teeth. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Exact tooth count and clutch interface dimensions are illustrative.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Exact tooth count and clutch interface dimensions are illustrative.

components.name: Timing covers
components.material: Cast aluminum · granular surface · machined fasteners
components.howItsMade: The front covers enclose the timing drive and retain lubricant. Moving them away reveals the chain route between the central drive and the two camshafts. Paired cast lids with raised perimeter lips, diagonal reinforcing ribs, circular bosses and separate perimeter fasteners. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Contours, raised ribs and bosses follow catalogue illustration 103-10; dimensions and exact aluminum alloy remain unverified.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Contours, raised ribs and bosses follow catalogue illustration 103-10; dimensions and exact aluminum alloy remain unverified.

components.name: Timing chains
components.material: Steel links · bright pins · dark sprocket faces
components.howItsMade: An intermediate drive turns two chains, one for each camshaft. Valve timing coordinates intake and exhaust events with piston travel through the four-stroke cycle. Two duplex linked paths, cam sprockets, guide rails, tensioner/idler assemblies and a longitudinal intermediate shaft. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Chain pitch, tensioner geometry and exact ratio are simplified; not a timing-setting reference.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Chain pitch, tensioner geometry and exact ratio are simplified; not a timing-setting reference.

components.name: Valve covers
components.howItsMade: The ribbed covers seal the valve mechanism. Removing them opens a service view of the rocker and cam assemblies beneath. Four elongated covers with rounded ends, raised ribs and perimeter fasteners. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Rib spacing, markings and gasket profiles are approximate.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Rib spacing, markings and gasket profiles are approximate.

components.name: Cam carriers
components.howItsMade: The carriers support the camshafts and rocker shafts along each bank. Alignment matters: a cam profile is useful only if the moving surfaces meet in the right place. Paired longitudinal structures with open bearing supports and upper/lower rails. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Carrier castings are simplified and not fully oil-tight solids.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Carrier castings are simplified and not fully oil-tight solids.

components.name: Camshafts
components.howItsMade: One overhead camshaft serves each bank. Its lobes act through rockers to open valves; spring force closes them after the lobe passes. Two shafts with six distinct lobes each; bearing journals remain visible in isolation. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Lobe lift and phase are illustrative rather than verified 901/01 cam profiles.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Lobe lift and phase are illustrative rather than verified 901/01 cam profiles.

components.name: Valves & rockers
components.material: Steel stems and springs · cast rocker finish
components.howItsMade: The intake valve admits fresh mixture; the exhaust valve lets spent gases leave. Rockers transmit cam motion, and springs keep the valves returning to their seats. Twelve poppet valves, stems, helical springs, retainers and rocker forms. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Exact rocker ratios and valve angles are not measured.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Exact rocker ratios and valve angles are not measured.

components.name: Ignition system
components.material: Brown insulating cap · black cable · pale ceramic
components.howItsMade: The distributor routes high voltage to six spark plugs. A spark starts combustion in the compressed mixture; the plug is a separate part of each head. Distributor body and cap, six cables, ceramic plug insulators and hexagonal bases. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Wire routing and plug details are representative; no exact firing-order claim.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Wire routing and plug details are representative; no exact firing-order claim.

components.name: Left crankcase
components.howItsMade: One half of the split crankcase supports the cylinders and the rotating shaft. The mating surfaces locate the other half and form the enclosed lower engine. Split shell with cylinder apertures, bearing supports, ribs and fastening bosses. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Casting shape and material grade are not established from measured factory data.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Casting shape and material grade are not established from measured factory data.

components.name: Right crankcase
components.howItsMade: The matching case half completes the main bearing supports. Bolting the halves together fixes the relationship between the crankshaft and both cylinder banks. Opposing shell with separate apertures, mating walls and support details. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Sealing geometry and oil passages are simplified.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Sealing geometry and oil passages are simplified.

components.name: Oil pump
components.howItsMade: The dry-sump system uses pumping stages to supply pressurized oil and scavenge it back toward a separate reservoir. Oil both lubricates moving interfaces and carries heat away. Sectioned pump housing exposes two paired gear stages; the inspection window is an educational cutaway. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: The permanent housing cutaway is illustrative; gear dimensions and hidden passages are schematic. The external oil tank is vehicle-mounted and not modeled.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. The permanent housing cutaway is illustrative; gear dimensions and hidden passages are schematic. The external oil tank is vehicle-mounted and not modeled.

components.name: Oil cooler
components.howItsMade: Oil carries heat from loaded surfaces to the cooler. Closely spaced fins give the air another route to remove that heat. Stacked thin cooler fins between end tanks at the rear of the engine. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Internal flow channels and exact fin pitch are unverified.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Internal flow channels and exact fin pitch are unverified.

components.name: Oil return & lines
components.material: Metal tubing · rubber hoses and seals · warm metal fittings
components.howItsMade: Return tubes carry oil from the heads back toward the case. External connections link the engine to the wider dry-sump circuit in the car. Rigid return tubes, separate seals, hose bends and hexagonal unions. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Routing is representative; the vehicle reservoir and filter are outside the model boundary.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Routing is representative; the vehicle reservoir and filter are outside the model boundary.

components.name: Exhaust system
components.howItsMade: Exhaust leaves each head through a runner, collects below the banks, and passes through the silencer. The cycle can then begin again with fresh mixture. Six curved runners, flange rings, transverse silencer, bands and outlet pipe. Manufacturing representation is illustrative: cast forms receive machined interfaces, while shafts, fasteners and sealing surfaces have distinct finishes.
funFacts: Heat exchangers, muffler baffles and exhaust wall thickness are simplified.

evidence.note: Function follows the documented architecture; dimensions and detailed contours are inferred. Heat exchangers, muffler baffles and exhaust wall thickness are simplified.

understanding.identityScope: 1965 Porsche 911 Type 901/01 air-cooled flat-six. Engine-mounted systems; vehicle ancillaries explicitly excluded.
learningGoals: Trace air and fuel into a cylinder, then force from piston to flywheel.
Explain how opposed cylinders differ from a V engine.
Distinguish cooling airflow from combustion intake airflow.
Connect valve timing to camshafts, rockers and chains.
Explain why an air-cooled engine still needs an oil circuit.

references.title: MS Road and Race: original 1965 aluminum chain-box covers
references.observation: Supplier listing identifies used early 911 chain housings/covers as aluminum. Text evidence; product photos were not inspected.
references.limitations: Supplier identification, not a factory alloy specification. Do not infer alloy grade or original surface treatment.

references.title: Porsche Classic 911/912 parts catalogue, MY1965–69
references.observation: Inspected diagrams 102-05 (crank/rods/flywheel), 103-00 (heads/cylinders/pistons), 103-10 (timing-cover raised borders, diagonal ribs and bolt bosses; PDF page 69), 103-15 (cam/rocker/chain/tensioner), 105-00 (fan/alternator/belt) and case diagram. Text distinguishes 911 from 912 and later variants.
references.limitations: Exploded diagrams are not measured drawings; catalogue spans several variants. Never use 912 parts as flat-six evidence.

references.title: Porsche: first generation 911
references.observation: Early rear-mounted, air-cooled six-cylinder engine and original 130 PS output.
references.limitations: History overview does not specify hidden geometry or manufacturing tolerances.

references.title: Historika: unrestored 1965 901/01 engine
references.observation: Viewed the front oblique engine photo: large front fan, three Solex throats on each bank, broad metal valve covers and dark shrouding.
references.limitations: Used condition; some photographs show the air cleaner removed. Do not copy grime into new metal or infer hidden geometry.

references.title: Restored 901/01: front and top reference photographs
references.observation: Inspected front and top photographs in Chrome. Silver fan ring and 11 blades, central belt, dark canopy, separated intake stacks, black wires and light grey transverse silencer.
references.limitations: Restoration may change finishes or components; listing identity is not factory verification.

references.title: Porsche 1966 sales brochure (archival scan)
references.observation: Period manufacturer description of overhead camshaft per bank and dry-sump lubrication with oil cooler.
references.limitations: Archival reproduction, adjacent model year. Does not establish dimensional fidelity.

inspectionGroups.name: Cylinder heads
inspectionGroups.description: Both banks close their cylinders with finned heads. Intake and exhaust valves control each chamber; the fins transfer heat into the cooling airflow.
inspectionGroups.material: Cast light alloy · machined valve seats

inspectionGroups.name: Cylinder banks
inspectionGroups.description: Three cylinders on each side form the opposed layout. The paired banks guide the six pistons, while their external fins shed heat to the fan-driven airflow.
inspectionGroups.material: Dark finned metal · bright mounting hardware

inspectionGroups.name: Crankcase halves
inspectionGroups.description: These two mating castings form one crankcase. Their bearing supports align around the crankshaft; their machined joint closes the structure beneath both cylinder banks.
inspectionGroups.material: Cast light alloy · machined mating faces

assemblyStory.title: From pressure to a flat-six.
assemblyStory.note: Educational build order, not a factory assembly or repair procedure. Geometry, finishes and hidden interfaces remain reference-fitted. Engine-mounted systems only; the external dry-sump tank and vehicle ancillaries are outside this model.

opening.title: Six cylinders. One engine.
opening.description: Meet the finished flat-six. Then follow its core outward: pressure becomes rotation, valves time each breath, and air and oil carry heat away. Each part returns to the growing engine.

closing.title: Every breath becomes motion.
closing.description: The finished engine brings the systems together: pistons turn the crankshaft, timed valves exchange gases, and cooling and lubrication keep the mechanism working. The external oil tank, fuel supply and vehicle connections complete it beyond this model.

chapters.title: Start with the turning core.
chapters.description: Six offset crankpins gather the piston forces into one rotating shaft. Main journals support it inside the case; counterweights help manage the rotating loads.
chapters.joined: The crankshaft is the reference around which the two opposed banks will grow.
chapters.detail: Steel shaft · polished journals · darker webs

chapters.title: Give each piston a connection.
chapters.description: Each rod connects a piston pin to its own crankpin. The big end follows a circle while the small end follows the piston, converting reciprocation into rotation.
chapters.joined: Six rods now link the crankpins to the future piston positions. Each big end follows the shaft; each small end follows a piston.
chapters.detail: Forged-metal appearance · polished bearing bores

chapters.title: Let pressure become force.
chapters.description: Combustion pressure pushes on each piston crown. Rings seal against the bore while the hollow skirt and wrist pin connect that force to a rod.
chapters.joined: The six pistons join their rods. Follow the load path from crown to wrist pin, rod and crankshaft.
chapters.detail: Machined light metal · darker ring bands

chapters.title: One path from pressure to rotation.
chapters.description: Seen together, the piston crowns, rods and offset crankpins explain the conversion: a straight push reaches a rotating shaft. This assembly pose shows the relationships; it is not a running simulation.
chapters.joined: The rotating core is ready for the structure that supports and guides it.
chapters.detail: Milestone · six piston–rod paths, one crankshaft

chapters.title: Support the core from both sides.
chapters.description: These two mating castings form one crankcase. Their bearing supports align around the crankshaft; their machined joint closes the structure beneath both cylinder banks.
chapters.joined: Both case halves seat around the rotating assembly. Their aligned supports give the shaft a stable structure.
chapters.detail: Cast light alloy · machined mating faces

chapters.title: Give the bearings an oil supply.
chapters.description: The dry-sump system uses pumping stages to supply pressurized oil and scavenge it back toward a separate reservoir. Oil both lubricates moving interfaces and carries heat away.
chapters.joined: The pump joins the core. Its pressure and scavenge roles belong to a dry-sump circuit whose external tank is outside this model.
chapters.detail: Cast housing · steel gear forms

chapters.title: Guide six pistons in opposed banks.
chapters.description: Three cylinders on each side form the opposed layout. The paired banks guide the six pistons, while their external fins shed heat to the fan-driven airflow.
chapters.joined: Both banks return together. Bores guide the pistons; the fins will later receive cooling airflow.
chapters.detail: Dark finned metal · bright mounting hardware

chapters.title: Close each combustion chamber.
chapters.description: Both banks close their cylinders with finned heads. Intake and exhaust valves control each chamber; the fins transfer heat into the cooling airflow.
chapters.joined: The paired heads close the cylinders. Their valve openings still need the moving parts that control each breath.
chapters.detail: Cast light alloy · machined valve seats

chapters.title: Open, close, and seal.
chapters.description: The intake valve admits fresh mixture; the exhaust valve lets spent gases leave. Rockers transmit cam motion, and springs keep the valves returning to their seats.
chapters.joined: Valves, springs and rockers take their places. They control gas exchange; the next parts determine when they move.
chapters.detail: Steel stems and springs · cast rocker finish

chapters.title: Keep the valve gear aligned.
chapters.description: The carriers support the camshafts and rocker shafts along each bank. Alignment matters: a cam profile is useful only if the moving surfaces meet in the right place.
chapters.joined: The carriers locate the cam and rocker supports along both banks.
chapters.detail: Cast housing · smooth bearing surfaces

chapters.title: Turn a profile into valve motion.
chapters.description: One overhead camshaft serves each bank. Its lobes act through rockers to open valves; spring force closes them after the lobe passes.
chapters.joined: Both camshafts return to their supports. Their lobes act through the rockers; spring force closes the valves.
chapters.detail: Steel · polished lobe surfaces

chapters.title: Connect valve events to piston travel.
chapters.description: An intermediate drive turns two chains, one for each camshaft. Valve timing coordinates intake and exhaust events with piston travel through the four-stroke cycle.
chapters.joined: The chain drive connects the crankshaft-side drive to both camshafts. These are illustrative positions, not timing marks for engine service.
chapters.detail: Steel links · bright pins · dark sprocket faces

chapters.title: A core that can time its own breathing.
chapters.description: The crankshaft, chain drive, camshafts and valve gear form one coordinated mechanism. The heads contain gas flow, the bores guide pistons, and the crankcase supports rotation. Intake, ignition and exhaust will give this mechanism its working connections.
chapters.joined: The timed core returns as one assembly. Now build the paths for mixture, spark and exhaust.
chapters.detail: Milestone · supported rotating core and timed valve gear

chapters.title: Carry rotation beyond the engine.
chapters.description: The flywheel stores rotational energy between firing impulses and passes torque toward the clutch. Its toothed perimeter also gives the starter a place to engage.
chapters.joined: The flywheel seats at the output end. The clutch and transmission would carry torque onward beyond this study.
chapters.detail: Machined steel · darker toothed rim

chapters.title: Build a route into each head.
chapters.description: The intake runners connect the carburetors to the cylinder heads. An intake valve admits the mixture into the chamber at the appropriate part of the cycle.
chapters.joined: Six intake runners connect the heads to the carburetors that follow.
chapters.detail: Cast-metal runners · machined flange faces

chapters.title: Meter the incoming mixture.
chapters.description: The early 901/01 uses Solex carburetion. Air passes through a throat for each cylinder; throttle position changes the flow and the carburetor meters fuel into it.
chapters.joined: The carburetors seat above the runners. Each cylinder now has a path for a metered air-fuel mixture.
chapters.detail: Cast alloy bodies · machined throats · brass fittings

chapters.title: Clean the air before it enters.
chapters.description: The air cleaner feeds the two banks of carburetors. Removing it reveals six separate intake throats beneath.
chapters.joined: The cleaner closes the intake path above the carburetors. This airflow feeds combustion, not the separate cooling fan.
chapters.detail: Satin black housing · bright fasteners

chapters.title: Add the spark.
chapters.description: The distributor routes high voltage to six spark plugs. A spark starts combustion in the compressed mixture; the plug is a separate part of each head.
chapters.joined: The distributor, leads and plugs complete the represented ignition path. Electrical timing and the running firing sequence are not simulated.
chapters.detail: Brown insulating cap · black cable · pale ceramic

chapters.title: Give spent gases a way out.
chapters.description: Exhaust leaves each head through a runner, collects below the banks, and passes through the silencer. The cycle can then begin again with fresh mixture.
chapters.joined: The exhaust returns below the banks, completing the represented route from intake to combustion to discharge.
chapters.detail: Heat-exposed metal · soft reflections

chapters.title: Follow one breath through the engine.
chapters.description: Air enters the cleaner and carburetors, mixture reaches the heads through the runners, ignition initiates combustion, and exhaust carries spent gases away. The valves you explored determine when the chambers connect to these paths.
chapters.joined: The breathing and ignition systems return to the core. Next, manage the heat that combustion produces.
chapters.detail: Milestone · intake, ignition and exhaust

chapters.title: Guide air across the hot engine.
chapters.description: The black shroud guides fan air over both cylinder banks. Without that guidance, air could escape before collecting heat from the fins.
chapters.joined: The shroud forms a separate air route over the finned cylinders and heads.
chapters.detail: Satin black finish · no baked highlights

chapters.title: Make electrical power from rotation.
chapters.description: Behind the fan, an alternator converts shaft rotation into electrical power. It shares the belt drive rather than needing a second motor.
chapters.joined: The alternator sits behind the fan position. Both share a belt-driven shaft arrangement.
chapters.detail: Cast housing · steel shaft

chapters.title: Support the fan and contain its inlet.
chapters.description: The housing supports the fan and alternator while keeping the blade tips close to the surrounding ring. It forms the inlet to the cooling duct.
chapters.joined: The housing seats around the alternator and the fan opening. Its ring defines the airflow entrance.
chapters.detail: Cast metal · restrained silver-grey reflection

chapters.title: Move air through the cooling route.
chapters.description: The pitched blades accelerate air into the shroud. Cooling needs directed flow across the hot surfaces, not simply an exposed engine.
chapters.joined: Eleven pitched blades return inside the housing. The fan directs air into the shroud instead of feeding combustion.
chapters.detail: Fine cast-metal finish · machined hub

chapters.title: Let the crankshaft drive the airflow.
chapters.description: The crankshaft turns a belt. That belt drives the cooling fan and alternator, so the running engine provides its own airflow.
chapters.joined: The belt links crankshaft rotation to the fan and alternator. The engine supplies its own cooling airflow.
chapters.detail: Machined metal pulleys · matte rubber belt

chapters.title: Carry away heat in the oil.
chapters.description: Oil carries heat from loaded surfaces to the cooler. Closely spaced fins give the air another route to remove that heat.
chapters.joined: The cooler rejoins the engine-mounted oil circuit. An air-cooled engine still needs lubrication and oil heat rejection.
chapters.detail: Metal fins · cast end tanks

chapters.title: Join the oil circuit together.
chapters.description: Return tubes carry oil from the heads back toward the case. External connections link the engine to the wider dry-sump circuit in the car.
chapters.joined: The represented lines return around the engine. The dry-sump circuit continues to an external tank not shown here.
chapters.detail: Metal tubing · rubber hoses and seals · warm metal fittings

chapters.title: Air and oil share the thermal work.
chapters.description: Fan-driven air travels over finned surfaces. Circulating oil lubricates loaded interfaces and carries heat toward the cooler. These routes complement each other; the external oil tank remains outside this engine model.
chapters.joined: Cooling and oil systems return. The final covers protect the working mechanisms.
chapters.detail: Milestone · directed cooling air and engine-mounted oil circuit

chapters.title: Close the chain drive.
chapters.description: The front covers enclose the timing drive and retain lubricant. Moving them away reveals the chain route between the central drive and the two camshafts.
chapters.joined: The cast covers seat over the chains. Their surfaces enclose the drive and retain lubricant.
chapters.detail: Cast aluminum · granular surface · machined fasteners

chapters.title: Close the service openings.
chapters.description: The ribbed covers seal the valve mechanism. Removing them opens a service view of the rocker and cam assemblies beneath.
chapters.joined: The covers seat over the valve mechanisms. The completed exterior now surrounds the detailed systems you have followed.
chapters.detail: Cast-metal covers · machined nuts
